title: Observability privacy middleware: deterministic token mapping and tiered archival policy
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Implement a privacy-focused middleware layer in the observability ingestion pipeline that applies deterministic token mapping (tenant-scoped hashing with controlled key rotation), enforces tiered archival (hot/warm/cold) for traces and logs, and logs all accesses to unhashed values via RBAC-bound audit entries. This ticket covers design updates, a PoC, policy enforcement hooks for sampling/burst scenarios, and integration with access logging and the console dashboards.

Motivation: Current pipelines persist raw trace/log payloads for 90 days which increases compliance risk and storage costs. Several customers have requested stronger guarantees: ability to provide hashed identifiers rather than raw PII, and clear, queryable audit trails for any actor who requests an unmasked value. We need a solution that: (1) preserves debugging utility for incident triage, (2) scales to peak telemetry volume, and (3) provides cryptographic controls for unmasking when operationally necessary.

Scope:
- Ingestion middleware library that runs in the trace/log pipeline (collector): applies tenant-scoped deterministic hashing for configured fields (email, user_id, phone) using per-tenant salt stored in KMS. Hashing must be reversible only via a key-access workflow (see "access_flow" below).
- Tiered archival policy enforcement:
  - Hot: full payloads for 7 days for recently ingested traces and any traces flagged as part of an active incident.
  - Warm: hashed payloads (no raw PII) for 30 days; KV cache retained for model-enrichment needs.
  - Cold: single-row aggregates and indexable metadata for 90+ days; raw payloads deleted or replaced by hashed equivalents.
- Access control + audit: any request to unhash a deterministic token must go through an RBAC check (console or API), produce an immutable audit record (actor, purpose, time, justification), and require KMS key unwrap via a short-lived credential. Audit logs are forwarded to an append-only ledger topic.
- Trace hooks and sampling interplay: add hook that marks traces for temporary hot retention when error-rate thresholds are crossed (e.g., >1% error spike per route) or for high-severity alerts. Hooks must be rate-limited and include TTL overrides that respect tenant policy.
- Console surfaces: add latency/error dashboard flags showing percent of traces redacted vs full and show access audit metrics per-tenant.

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Deterministic hashing increases ability to correlate repeated identifiers across events without storing the raw value. We must rotate tenant salts on schedule; rotations will change mapping and complicate long-term correlation. We will store rotation metadata to allow short-term rehydrate windows where allowed.
- Reversible unmasking introduces attack surface. To mitigate: ephemeral KMS unwrapping for authorized requests only, ephemeral credentials, and rate-limiting + multi-approval for high-sensitivity unmasking. This requires security review.
- Performance: hashing must add <1ms p50 to ingestion path under normal load. We'll implement native bindings (Rust) for the collector plugin and benchmark on representative workloads.

Acceptance Criteria: [list]
- Middleware PoC that hashes configured fields using tenant-scoped salt; unit/integration tests for mapping correctness.
- End-to-end pipeline test showing hot/warm/cold transitions for a synthetic traffic pattern.
- RBAC-backed unmask flow implemented with an audit entry per unmask request; audit entries visible in the append-only ledger.
- Grafana dashboard updated to show redaction ratios and an access-event heatmap.
- Performance tests demonstrating <1ms p50 overhead and <2ms p95 on baseline infra.

Technical links: [list]
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Deterministic+Token+Mapping+Design
- Collector PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector-privacy-proxy (PRs below)
- KMS integration spec: https://internal.redwood.ai/specs/kms-unwrap-workflow
acceptance_criteria: PoC collector plugin hashes configured fields with per-tenant salt and has unit + integration tests
End-to-end test demonstrates hot->warm->cold lifecycle for synthetic traces
RBAC unmask API creates immutable audit record that appears in ledger topic
Grafana dashboard includes redaction ratio and access-event heatmap
Performance regression tests: <1ms p50, <2ms p95 added latency at baseline
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy PoC in staging with a small subset of tenants behind feature flag (2 weeks). Phase 2: opt-in beta for 5 low-latency tenants to validate perf and operations (3 weeks). Phase 3: gradual ramp with per-tenant policy defaults and console controls; full rollout gated on security review and SRE signoff (target release observability-2025.03).
testing_plan: Unit tests for hash mapping and rotation, integration test in CI that runs the collector plugin + pipeline, load test with synthetic high-throughput traces to validate latency, chaos test to validate KMS unavailability fallback (deny-by-default), e2e test for unmask workflow including audit record verification.
